title: improve-response-schema-error-taxonomy-and-openai-compat-behavior
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: customers using response_format="schema" together with the OpenAI compatibility layer reported confusing errors during streaming responses and tool calls; some errors were opaque (generic 500-style messages) and made retry/rollback logic brittle. This PR introduces a clearer error taxonomy and small behavioral changes so clients can make deterministic decisions in strict vs permissive modes. Summary of changes: 1) Define a concise error taxonomy returned in the inference response envelope when response_format="schema" is used (keys: structure.mismatch, schema.partial, stream.truncation, toolcall.fenced, compat.narrowing). 2) When running in openai_compat mode we map legacy error shapes (old openai-like error.body) to the new taxonomy and include a compat_hint header for clients migrating from the OpenAI shape. 3) Streaming path: introduced a finalization signal ("schema_finalized": true/false) in the non-streaming envelope and a stream footer event in streaming mode that gives a deterministic schema validation result; this avoids ambiguous client-side timeouts deciding whether to attempt a resume. 4) Tool/function-calling: we add an explicit fence error (toolcall.fenced) when the model returns a tool invocation that violates the declared tool contract (missing required fields or wrong return type) and include a recommended action (retry_with_prompt_fix / abort) to help orchestration layers. 5) Backwards compatibility: default behavior in permissive mode remains unchanged; strict mode flips on both runtime enforcement and the new error codes.

Checklist: - [x] Define error code strings and schema for envelope (docs + enum). - [x] Implement mapping layer in openai adapter. - [x] Add stream footer event and resume hint implementation. - [x] Add tests for strict/permissive behavior and toolcall fencing. - [x] Update SDK error docs and quickstart example.

Design notes: - Error envelope lives at inference response top-level under "schema_validation" and carries: code, message, details (array of short strings), and hint (retry, abort, fallback-model). To keep JSON response small during streaming we emit a compact footer event: {event: "schema_result", code:..., hint:...}. - For OpenAI compatibility we continue to accept legacy error responses but always emit a compat_hint header that includes the new code equivalent. This avoids client breakages while nudging teams to adopt the richer codes.

Migration guide: clients should prefer the new codes when present. For streaming clients, wait for the final footer event before marking schema check success/failure; if the connection drops before the footer is received, the client may reconnect using the provided resume_token (if present) or fall back to the permissive path.

Security and performance considerations: schema validation runs in a lightweight sandbox and is guarded by a short-circuiting fast-path (prefix checks) to avoid full validation on common OK responses. The added validation accounts for ~2% median CPU increase on our canary but reduces downstream error churn.

Risks: clients that depended on parsing human-readable error messages in the past will need to migrate to the structured codes; the PR includes a compat mapping to reduce disruption.

review_comments: Jordan Patel: Please clarify how stream.truncation differs from partial schema failures. In particular, when clients reconnect do they need to re-run validation from scratch?

Maya Chen (author): stream.truncation is reserved for when the streaming connection closed without a footer event. We include a resume_token; reconnecting with the token jumps to validation continuation so clients do not need to re-run from scratch in most cases.
Lena Sørensen: Can we avoid extra latency in the hot path? The perf numbers look OK but please add a percentile breakdown and a stress test for long sequences.

Maya Chen (author): Added percentile breakdown to the canary job and a stress test for >8k token sequences. Observed 1.8-2.4% CPU overhead p50/p95 respectively; added opt-out config knob for ultra-latency-sensitive customers.
Ravi Kapoor: Toolcall fence behavior seems a little strict for some legacy tools — can we provide a tolerant mode?

Maya Chen (author): Added a permissive_tool_fence config flag that downgrades fence errors to a schema.partial with a details array containing missing fields; also documented recommended action mappings.
Lena Sørensen: Docs look good; add a short example showing SDK handling of the new codes.
Maya Chen (author): Added example snippets to sdk/python/redwood/schema_errors.py and the JS quickstart.

release_notes: Added structured error taxonomy for response_format="schema" (structure.mismatch, schema.partial, toolcall.fenced, stream.truncation, compat.narrowing). Streaming now emits a compact footer event with final validation result; OpenAI compatibility layer maps legacy errors to the new codes and includes a compat_hint header. Migration guidance available in docs/api/response_schema.md.

changelog_entry: 2026-02-25: Introduce schema validation error taxonomy and streaming footer. OpenAI adapter maps legacy errors to new codes. Added SDK enums and migration docs.
notes_for_ops: Ops: rollout uses canary sampler controlled by charts/helm values:validationSamplingRate. There is a config flag permissive_tool_fence for downgrading fence errors during rollout. Monitor metric schema.validation.errors.by_code and streaming.footer.missing_count for initial 24h post-deploy.
migration_guide: Clients: prefer checking schema_validation.code in the response; fallback to compat_hint or legacy openai error.body when code missing. For streaming, wait for schema_result footer or use resume_token to reconnect. SDKs provide helpers to map codes to recommended_action.
additional_context: This PR was coordinated with SDK and docs teams to minimize breaking changes; the goal is to make schema validation actionable for orchestration layers (canary rollouts, automated retries, and tool fences) without degrading latency for common success paths.
